requirement:
YAML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment,
including a comment following a mapping value. A `#` within quoted text or
within the content of a block scalar belongs to the scalar.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.attachments` has no structural obligations, so it needs no implementation evidence. It has a test edge but no implementation edge. I did not read the test source, because test adequacy is outside this assessment.

I checked each clause for an implementation choice it prescribes:
- "YAML reports only `Comment` attachments" limits which attachment kinds the YAML source reports. That is output behavior. A parser built differently, such as a hand-written scanner or a different YAML library, could report the same kinds and still meet the clause. It names no library, signature, type or interface.
- "Each `#` comment is one attachment, including a comment following a mapping value" says what counts as an attachment. That is also output behavior.
- "A `#` within quoted text or within the content of a block scalar belongs to the scalar" is a lexical rule about what is and isn't a comment. It is also output behavior.

Every clause describes what is observed, and none prescribes how the code is built. The requirement is non-distributed and its obligations are behavioral, which tests cover. No root needs an `{impl}` marker.

behavioral: The only test is `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. Its `test.yaml` case uses the source `a: |\n  # literal\n# standalone\nb: '# literal' # real\nc: "# literal"\n`. The test builds the outline, collects every attachment on every item, and compares the full list of (kind, trimmed span text) pairs with `[(Comment, "# standalone"), (Comment, "# real")]`. That is an exact comparison.

Obligations mapped to this case:
- **Only `Comment` attachments.** Every expected pair has kind `Comment`, and the comparison is exact, so any other kind would fail it.
- **Each `#` comment is one attachment.** `# standalone` and `# real` each appear as their own attachment, with the span text checked.
- **A comment following a mapping value counts.** `b: '# literal' # real` yields `# real`.
- **A `#` in a block scalar belongs to the scalar.** The literal block `a: |` containing `# literal` yields no attachment.
- **A `#` in quoted text belongs to the scalar.** The single-quoted `'# literal'` and the double-quoted `"# literal"` yield none. The single-quoted one is also followed by a real comment, which is still found.

The exact-list comparison catches both missed comments and spurious ones. I found no behavioral obligation without a scenario. I did not treat folded block scalars (`>`) or adjacent YAML comments as gaps, because the requirement does not single them out.
